review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read EqToHom.lean for eqToHom_refl, eqToHom_trans and eqToHom_naturality, and HomologicalComplex.lean for d_comp_eqToHom and eqToHom_comp_d. I grepped for uses of objEqToHom, eqToHom_f' and d_eqToHom. The non-simp status of objEqToHom_d and eqToHom_f' is deliberate and documented as avoiding a loop against eqToHom_naturality, so I did not flag it. d_eqToHom is unused outside this file; I did not report it because a simp attribute there would be speculative. I could not run Lean, so the redundancy of objEqToHom_refl rests on reading the sources. It depends on simp seeing through the reducible abbrev and on eqToHom_refl matching an arbitrary proof argument.

findings.problem: `objEqToHom` is an `abbrev`, so it is reducible and simp's discrimination tree unfolds it. The docstring says the definition "is used to aid the simplifier", but `X.objEqToHom (refl i)` is already the term `eqToHom congr(X.obj $(refl i))`. The existing simp lemma `eqToHom_refl` already rewrites this to `𝟙 _` for any proof `p : X = X`. The `@[simp]` lemma therefore looks like a redundant duplicate of `eqToHom_refl`. A simpNF-style check would likely report its LHS as simplifiable by another simp lemma. The docstring also gives a misleading reason for the abbrev.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `objEqToHom_refl` or drop its `@[simp]` attribute, relying on `eqToHom_refl`. If `X.objEqToHom` is wanted as a distinct simp head, make it a plain `def` and keep a dedicated simp lemma. Otherwise reword the docstring so it does not claim that the abbrev helps the simplifier.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical rule for the identity case instead of two overlapping ones. The simp set stays smaller. The docstring no longer suggests that `objEqToHom` is opaque to simp when it is reducible.
